title: Move Zeroes
description:
Rearrange nums in place so that all nonzero values appear first, in their original relative order, followed by all the zeros. Return the modified array. The return value is what this exercise grades; changing the array without returning it is not enough.

A write position for the next nonzero value separates the part you have already compacted from the untouched part. The interesting constraint is preserving order while avoiding another array of the same size.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [0,1,0,3,12]
Output: [1,3,12,0,0]

Example 2:

Input: nums = [0]
Output: [0]

Example 3:

Input: nums = [4,0,-2,0,5]
Output: [4,-2,5,0,0]

Constraints:

  • 1 <= nums.length <= 10,000
  • -1,000,000 <= nums[i] <= 1,000,000
  • Modify nums in place and use O(1) auxiliary space.

exampleTestCases.explanation: The nonzeros retain their order, followed by two zeros.
A single zero is already in place.
The negative value is nonzero and stays between 4 and 5.
